<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD is a standard binary package that downloads a .deb from the project's official GitHub releases (https://github.com/Kesomannen/gale/releases). The source array includes a local patch file with a SKIP checksum, which is normal for patches shipped in the AUR repo. No top-level command substitution, no `pkgver()` function, and no code executes during sourcing other than variable assignments. The `package()` and `post_*` functions are not invoked by `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` or `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. Fetching and extracting the upstream binary artifact is exactly what these commands are designed to do; a missing or SKIPped checksum on the patch does not make this step unsafe.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>Standard binary package; no malicious code in fetch/sourcing phase.</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This is a standard AUR binary package (`-bin`) for the Gale Thunderstore client. The source downloads the upstream `.deb` from the project's own GitHub releases page (`https://github.com/Kesomannen/gale/releases/download/...`), which is expected behavior. The `.deb` file is properly pinned with a SHA256 checksum, while the local patch file uses `SKIP` (acceptable for a local patch).

The `package()` function performs the standard extraction of `data.tar.gz` from the Debian package into `${pkgdir}` and applies a local patch (`webkit-disable-compositing.patch`) — a routine practice for WebKit2GTK applications to address compositing issues. The post-install/upgrade/remove hooks only call standard system cache update utilities (`gtk-update-icon-cache`, `update-desktop-database`), which are ordinary post-install operations for GTK-based GUI applications.

No suspicious network activity, obfuscated code, data exfiltration, or execution of external scripts is present. All dependencies are standard GTK/WebKit2GTK libraries appropriate for the application's stated purpose.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Standard AUR binary package with no security concerns.</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for update-pkgbuild.sh:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The script `update-pkgbuild.sh` is a conventional AUR maintainer helper. It fetches release metadata from the official GitHub repository **Kesomannen/gale**, extracts the version, download URL, and checksum of the Debian package (`amd64.deb`), downloads the package, and updates the local `PKGBUILD` (adjusting `pkgver` and `sha256sums_x86_64`). All network requests target the declared upstream source, and the script performs routine post‑download maintenance (removing the temporary `.deb` file). No obfuscation, unexpected external connections, or execution of untrusted code is observed.

While the script directly modifies `PKGBUILD` with `sed` and uses `wget` (which may not be present on all systems), these actions are standard practices for AUR package maintenance. No evidence of data exfiltration, reverse shells, or injected malicious payloads is found.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Standard AUR update script with no malicious behavior.
</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for webkit-disable-compositing.patch:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This is a standard patch file that modifies a desktop entry file for the Gale mod manager application. The change simply prepends `WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE=1` to the `Exec` command, which is a well-known environment variable used to disable GPU compositing in WebKit-based applications. This is a legitimate performance/compatibility tweak commonly used to address rendering issues in virtual machines or with certain graphics drivers. The patch does not perform any network operations, file exfiltration, or execute any untrusted code.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Legitimate desktop entry patch for WebKit performance tuning</summary>
</security_assessment>
